Retirement Home Neglect [5974]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Production

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
18th April Proposals – Flame Lily Park – Elder Abuse



1. Flame Lily Park



is a retirement village in Queensborough.



Peggy Bailey was a 95 year old resident living in assisted care. She was very sprightly and was the first to go to breakfast in the mornings. She would be there by 7 am and open all the curtains. Two weeks before Easter her grand daughter Caitlin took her to Sorbet and they both had pedicures. She was very animated and was able to get into a hilux bakkie quite easily.

That was the last time her grand daughter saw her conscious.

It is believed that she fell in her bath room at Flame Lily where she was living in assisted care.

No-one looked in to see if she was alright for 8 days.

The family had not heard from her and they phoned the retirement centre a couple of times and asked the receptionsist to check up on her. But the receptionist forgot.

The found her 8 days later, barely conscious. The staff at Flame Lily cleaned her and the room and she was rushed to the hospital . When the doctors saw her they were concerned that she had been raped because she had infections and pus. There was brown matter in her mouth.



She had a bruises on her head, very bad bed sore on her back and was exceptionally dehydrated. She was rushed to Hillcrest Hospital and put on a ventilator.

The doctors did a preliminary investigation and found that she was not raped but just in a terrible state of neglect due to being severly dehydrated.

The family decided to take her off ventilation and she survived for 3 more days and passed away on Saturday morning.



Later last year the family moved her from her flatlet into assisted care because she could not see that well and they paid extra for assisted living care for her.



The family is completely devastated. How could she have been left in her room for 8 days without anyone noticing she was missing.

The family has arranged for Reggie Perumal to do the autopsy and he will share his findings with me.



The family is willing to speak to me. They are obviously very traumatised.



They tried during that time to phone and find out how their mother was as they had not heard from her and no-one came back to her.



The point of the story is that one puts elderly in homes hoping that they will receive the loving care that they need but this is not always the case.



There is no governing body or ethical organisation of retirement establishments.



What steps does one have to take to make sure your parents are well cared for? Katherine’s cousins put cameras in their parents home and they could watch their parents and interact with them.



They noticed one of the nurses was quite rough with her parents and she was fired by the establishment.



A friend of ours is the general manager of the faciulity where Katherine’s parents stay and they have a 3 fold alert system. Residents wear panic buttons. The cleaners check everyday and they are noticed when they do not come down for meals.



Can you imagine what this old woman must have felt like lying on the cold floor for 8 days alone? Her next door neighbour thought she heard someone scratching or calling but forgot to tell someone.



Interviews



Celia – Daughter of Peggy who died on weekend.
Caitlin - Peggy's granddaughter who saw her last

Henry Spenser - Stays in independent living old age home. Has written 10 books on subject material. Invented buddy system.
Was managed at TAFTA for several years and ran 8 retirement homes in UK. Expert in gerontological matters.

Syd Eckley - South African Older Person's Forum. Chair. Highly knowledgeable about laws and current situation with lack of supervision at retirement homes.


Terry Sterling – Manager of Garden Grove in Durban.

Script – Flame Lily Elder Neglect Edit 11

Up Sound

Celia
“On Monday the 9th of August it will be 4 months since my mother was found in a horrific state on the floor of her bathroom, in the assisted living facility of the Flame Lily Frail Care. And according to the doctors, treating her later that day, having been there for almost a week.”

V/O
This is a letter written by Celia Bayley asking the management of a Durban retirement home, to please communicate with her and tell her how it was possible for her 95 year old mother to collapse and fall on her bathroom floor and no-one noticed she was missing.

Link
“This is the Flame Lily Park Retirement Village it was established by the Memorable Order of Tin Hats or Moths. It offers low cost accommodation to people over the age of 60 and this is where Peggy Chandler spent more than 20 years of her life.”

Up Sound ‘You know who is a softie with animals?”

V/O 00:55
Peggy Chandler was a sprightly 95 year old, this video of her was taken at the beginning of this year. She lived a full life and was the matriarch of a loving supportive family. Up until two years ago she lived very happily in the independent units at Flame Lily Park and was totally self-sufficient.
Her daughter Celia Bayley lives in Johannesburg, says her mother was able to cook for herself and clean her own flatlet.

Masa
“She lived in an independent unit and then moved to assisted living – why is that?”

Celia
“In 2019 when she was with us over Christmas she said she was tired and assisted living was to give her 3 meals a day and washing done once a week and then also clean her room once a week.”






V/O
This was Peggy’s room in assisted living and this is the bathroom that she lay unassisted in her own vomit and faeces for about a week.

Femada Shamam is the CEO of TAFTA, The Association for the Aged, that offers about 1500 people housing in Durban. South Africa recognises that the elderly are vulnerable members of our society, and protects them in law through the Older Persons Act.

Femada
“So these rights are fundamental to older people to ensure that they age with dignity and age with respect, age with all that they need to age with in order for them to have meaningful lives.”

V/O
There are about 5 million people of retirement age in South Africa. The government encourages home based care for the elderly but some choose the security of retirement villages or old age homes, where they know they will get the medical care they need, when they become less able to look after themselves.

Link
There are various options when it comes to retirement homes, there is independent living where you can look after yourself, there is frail care where one gets 24 hours a day assistance, and then there is the one in-between assisted living.

Henry
“If you ask a person what is assisted living you will get a dozen answers?”

V/O
Henry Spencer is a gerontologist and has first-hand experience in running retirement homes here and abroad. He lives in an independent unit in a retirement complex in Pietermaritzburg.

Masa
“What would you say people should look out for when they are looking for a retirement village?”

Henry
“They should ask all the right questions, they should try and speak to people who know the home very well and not just sales people.”

V/O
It is the last home that many people will live in and Henry Spencer says it is vital that prospective residents check the references of the institution and speak to people who live there, to make sure they make an informed Old Age homes need to be compliant with regulations set out by the law.

Henry
“It’s a one way street, and if you get it wrong it’s hard to come back.”

Femada
“There are very specific regulations around frail care but in terms of assisted living it is not that regulated, and it is left to the individual organisations to manage the assisted living units within the processes of that particular organisation.

V/O
When Peggy Chandler moved from the independent flatlets to assisted living she paid about R 5000 more for the added services.

Celia
“My mother had signed a contract, it’s a one page document that says that she would have her room cleaned and her laundry done and her meals supplied. I expected that they would make sure that she was safe.”

V/O
The contract did not state that she would be checked daily, and the cleaning staff only went to Peggy Chandler’s room once a week.

Because of COVID, Flame Lily Park, went into lockdown.
It was around Easter this year, when Celia Bayley believes that her mother fell in her bathroom and lay alone on the cold floor with no food or water and no one to help her. Her family called the phone in her room several times and eventually in desperation asked the home to look for her. When the matron found her she was unconscious. Peggy Chandler was rushed to hospital in a critical state and her daughter flew down from Johannesburg to be at her side.







Masa
“Was she able to speak?”

Celia
“No, my mom I don’t know how but her nails were totally caked in whatever she had been lying in. She had massive trauma, brusing on her shoulders , she had a pressure sore of about 15cm square on her lower back and the doctor said that it had gone all the way through to her spine.”

V/O
Her family was holding vigil at the hospital, but Peggy Chandler would not release her hold on life.

Celia
“And then I said to her, you can’t do this to us anymore.”

V/O
A week after she was found, she succumbed to her injuries.

Pause

Liana Grobler is an advocate for the elderly and heads up the South African Association of Homes for the Aged or SAAHA, an organisation which assists legislative compliance of 300 homes across the country. In her opinion, what happened to Peggy Chandler was a complete dereliction of the duty to care.

Liana
“I can clearly state to you that it is unacceptable from a personal and association point of view she shouldn’t have been without care for at least a day, that’s minimum. So if she fell today she should have been found the next day.”




V/O
The contract that Peggy Chandler signed was only a couple of lines long and did not mention daily care.
Liana Grobler says that one must pay special attention to contracts when moving from one kind of care to another in the same institution to see exactly what is provided.

Liana
My proposal would be to look at the nursing care and security and then if you have any doubts, I would actually take that contract and have that looked at by my own attorney before signature because when one moves from one type of care to another type of care you actually need to sign a new contract.”

V/O
We posed as prospective new residents at Flame Lily and spoke to the person in charge of letting.

Steve
“Assisted living is where they make sure you go for your meal, you see semi frail is where they check up on you all the time, they make sure you are OK, they check up on you, but assisted living is you on your own, you must then go for yourself for lunch, breakfast, whatever it is, that is assisted living.”

V/O
But no-one at Flame Lily Park reported that Peggy Chandler was not at any of the meals.

Link
Many of these institutions have systems in place to monitor the residents daily, one of the most popular is the buddy system.

V/O
The idea is a clever one at night residents put a disk on their door to say that they have gone to sleep, in the morning they remove it. If it is not removed, neighbours will see it and call for help. Similarly it should be noticed if you don’t put the disk out at night. At most, if something happened to one of the residents, it would be noticed within 12 hours.


When we were shown around Flame Lily Park they had a similar system for independent living that Peggy Chandler had used for 20 years, but oddly not for assisted living.



Flame Lily Park Man
“In the morning when you wake up, you turn your disk so it faces brown and at night before you go to bed it faces yellow, and we have 1 block rep on each floor that will walk around to see that the resident has turned their disk, if they haven’t turned their disk then they will know on the door to find out why they haven’t turned their disk.”

V/O

We requested an interview with Flame Lily Park to try and get some answers.

The establishment declined an on camera interview but sent a statement.

It said that it was difficult to check up on Peggy because she often locked herself in her room and was abusive if people disturbed her.

Flame Lily Park admitted that there was no disk system in the section where Peggy stayed because the section had opened during COVID and there were only had 2 residents in that area.

Masa
“If you are going to pay more for a service because initially she was living in a cottage but there was a system to check that she was alive on a daily basis then moves to a better care facility within the home and they don’t check on her daily?”

Henry
“It sounds very strange. You would think that if they had come from that system of living independently that it should continue at least in the new more cared for area where she was.”





V/O
The home admitted that it relied on the hearsay of a resident who said that Peggy would be away for the Easter weekend – even though she had not signed out. “There is a system but due to the Covid pandemic the system was dormant with very few residents leaving and re-entering unless for medical reasons.”

V/O
Shamam says thaTAFTA is not immune to accidents but she says that they work together with the families to resolve the problems.

Famada
“When you are dealing with people the margin of error is always present, so you have to minimise the risk and where things have not gone the way that they need to happen, you need to be able to say OK, lets investigate this, lets understand what is happening and hold people accountable.”

V/O
The Department of Social Development requires retirement homes to report incidents and accidents that happen to residents. Krish Shanmugam is KZN’s Director of the Special Needs programme which includes Older Persons.

Masa
“How long does it usually take once a complaint has been lodged by the department to reach your level?”

Krish
“If there is a complain of abuse or neglect the complain is received immediately within the province, wth our department to respond to.”

V/O
This incident occurred over Easter but the Department only received the report 4 months later.

Krish
“We were not notified of this case other wise we would have responded immediately.”

Masa
“What are the repercussions when a facility is alleged for neglect and they don’t report such incidents?”

Krish
“It’s an offence. It’ll be treated as a criminal offence.”

V/O
In a statement Flame Lily Park has said that they will cooperate with all official investigations into Peggy Chandler’s incident and they are waiting for the Department of Social Developments official written query and will answer their questions.
But Flame Lily Park has not contacted Peggy Chandler’s family since her death, to provide any answers to the questions posed in the letter that was sent.

Celia
In modern terminology my mother has been ghosted by all those whose responsibility it was to have insured that her declining years were of safety care and comfort and in whom she placed her trust.

Celia
“The treatment that my mother received was worse than an abandoned dog and we feel that as a family we also feel equally abandoned by an organisation that purports to care.”


Promo 1 x 11 sec

After falling in her bathroom in an old age home in Durban, a 95 year old lady lay alone on the floor without food or water for about a week before someone found her.

Promo 2 x 21 sec

V/O
95 year old Peggy Chandler lived in assisted living in a retirement in Durban

“All I expected was that they would check on my mother.”

But no one did, Peggy fell in her bathroom and was left lying on the floor with no food or water for about a week.


Promo 3 x 21 sec

V/O
After spending 22 years in an retirement home, a 95 year old woman was left lying alone in her bathroom for about a week.

“The treatment that my mother received was worse than an abandoned dog and we feel as a family equally abandoned.”

Steve “Assisted living is where they make sure you go for your meal, you see semi frail is where they check up on you all the time, they make sure you are OK, they check up on you, but assisted living is you on your own, you must then go for yourself for lunch, breakfast, whatever it is, that is assisted living.” V/O But no-one at Flame Lily Park reported that Peggy Chandler was not at any of the meals. Link Many of these institutions have systems in place to monitor the residents daily, one of the most popular is the buddy system. V/O The idea is a clever one at night residents put a disk on their door to say that they have gone to sleep, in the morning they remove it. If it is not removed, neighbours will see it and call for help. Similarly it should be noticed if you don’t put the disk out at night. At most, if something happened to one of the residents, it would be noticed within 12 hours. When we were shown around Flame Lily Park they had a similar system for independent living that Peggy Chandler had used for 20 years, but oddly not for assisted living. Flame Lily Park Man “In the morning when you wake up, you turn your disk so it faces brown and at night before you go to bed it faces yellow, and we have 1 block rep on each floor that will walk around to see that the resident has turned their disk, if they haven’t turned their disk then they will know on the door to find out why they haven’t turned their disk.” V/O We requested an interview with Flame Lily Park to try and get some answers. The establishment declined an on camera interview but sent a statement. It said that it was difficult to check up on Peggy because she often locked herself in her room and was abusive if people disturbed her. Flame Lily Park admitted that there was no disk system in the section where Peggy stayed because the section had opened during COVID and there were only had 2 residents in that area. Masa “If you are going to pay more for a service because initially she was living in a cottage but there was a system to check that she was alive on a daily basis then moves to a better care facility within the home and they don’t check on her daily?” Henry “It sounds very strange. You would think that if they had come from that system of living independently that it should continue at least in the new more cared for area where she was.” V/O The home admitted that it relied on the hearsay of a resident who said that Peggy would be away for the Easter weekend – even though she had not signed out. “There is a system but due to the Covid pandemic the system was dormant with very few residents leaving and re-entering unless for medical reasons.” V/O Shamam says thaTAFTA is not immune to accidents but she says that they work together with the families to resolve the problems. Famada “When you are dealing with people the margin of error is always present, so you have to minimise the risk and where things have not gone the way that they need to happen, you need to be able to say OK, lets investigate this, lets understand what is happening and hold people accountable.” V/O The Department of Social Development requires retirement homes to report incidents and accidents that happen to residents. Krish Shanmugam is KZN’s Director of the Special Needs programme which includes Older Persons. Masa “How long does it usually take once a complaint has been lodged by the department to reach your level?” Krish “If there is a complain of abuse or neglect the complain is received immediately within the province, wth our department to respond to.” V/O This incident occurred over Easter but the Department only received the report 4 months later. Krish “We were not notified of this case other wise we would have responded immediately.” Masa “What are the repercussions when a facility is alleged for neglect and they don’t report such incidents?” Krish “It’s an offence. It’ll be treated as a criminal offence.” V/O In a statement Flame Lily Park has said that they will cooperate with all official investigations into Peggy Chandler’s incident and they are waiting for the Department of Social Developments official written query and will answer their questions. But Flame Lily Park has not contacted Peggy Chandler’s family since her death, to provide any answers to the questions posed in the letter that was sent. Celia In modern terminology my mother has been ghosted by all those whose responsibility it was to have insured that her declining years were of safety care and comfort and in whom she placed her trust. Celia “The treatment that my mother received was worse than an abandoned dog and we feel that as a family we also feel equally abandoned by an organisation that purports to care.” Promo 1 x 11 sec After falling in her bathroom in an old age home in Durban, a 95 year old lady lay alone on the floor without food or water for about a week before someone found her. Promo 2 x 21 sec V/O 95 year old Peggy Chandler lived in assisted living in a retirement in Durban “All I expected was that they would check on my mother.” But no one did, Peggy fell in her bathroom and was left lying on the floor with no food or water for about a week. Promo 3 x 21 sec V/O After spending 22 years in an retirement home, a 95 year old woman was left lying alone in her bathroom for about a week. “The treatment that my mother received was worse than an abandoned dog and we feel as a family equally abandoned.”

metadata.Further information: 18th April Proposals – Flame Lily Park – Elder Abuse 1. Flame Lily Park is a retirement village in Queensborough. Peggy Bailey was a 95 year old resident living in assisted care. She was very sprightly and was the first to go to breakfast in the mornings. She would be there by 7 am and open all the curtains. Two weeks before Easter her grand daughter Caitlin took her to Sorbet and they both had pedicures. She was very animated and was able to get into a hilux bakkie quite easily. That was the last time her grand daughter saw her conscious. It is believed that she fell in her bath room at Flame Lily where she was living in assisted care. No-one looked in to see if she was alright for 8 days. The family had not heard from her and they phoned the retirement centre a couple of times and asked the receptionsist to check up on her. But the receptionist forgot. The found her 8 days later, barely conscious. The staff at Flame Lily cleaned her and the room and she was rushed to the hospital . When the doctors saw her they were concerned that she had been raped because she had infections and pus. There was brown matter in her mouth. She had a bruises on her head, very bad bed sore on her back and was exceptionally dehydrated. She was rushed to Hillcrest Hospital and put on a ventilator. The doctors did a preliminary investigation and found that she was not raped but just in a terrible state of neglect due to being severly dehydrated. The family decided to take her off ventilation and she survived for 3 more days and passed away on Saturday morning. Later last year the family moved her from her flatlet into assisted care because she could not see that well and they paid extra for assisted living care for her. The family is completely devastated. How could she have been left in her room for 8 days without anyone noticing she was missing. The family has arranged for Reggie Perumal to do the autopsy and he will share his findings with me. The family is willing to speak to me. They are obviously very traumatised. They tried during that time to phone and find out how their mother was as they had not heard from her and no-one came back to her. The point of the story is that one puts elderly in homes hoping that they will receive the loving care that they need but this is not always the case. There is no governing body or ethical organisation of retirement establishments. What steps does one have to take to make sure your parents are well cared for? Katherine’s cousins put cameras in their parents home and they could watch their parents and interact with them. They noticed one of the nurses was quite rough with her parents and she was fired by the establishment. A friend of ours is the general manager of the faciulity where Katherine’s parents stay and they have a 3 fold alert system. Residents wear panic buttons. The cleaners check everyday and they are noticed when they do not come down for meals. Can you imagine what this old woman must have felt like lying on the cold floor for 8 days alone? Her next door neighbour thought she heard someone scratching or calling but forgot to tell someone. Interviews Celia – Daughter of Peggy who died on weekend. Caitlin - Peggy's granddaughter who saw her last Henry Spenser - Stays in independent living old age home. Has written 10 books on subject material. Invented buddy system. Was managed at TAFTA for several years and ran 8 retirement homes in UK. Expert in gerontological matters. Syd Eckley - South African Older Person's Forum. Chair. Highly knowledgeable about laws and current situation with lack of supervision at retirement homes. Terry Sterling – Manager of Garden Grove in Durban. Flame Lily Chairman Mobile Email Chairman Chris Craig-mackie 082 681 9244 chris61.cm@gmail.com Reggie Perumal – autoposy report. Will also pose as someone who wants to bring mother to stay in facility and ask about care.
